command: python3 -m scorer.judge report --labels labels/set1.jsonl --final labels/set1-final.jsonl --readings labels/set1-readings.json --provenance labels/set1-provenance.txt --verdicts judgments/set1-llama3.1-8b
provenance: Written by Claude, in the PM seat, at the owner's request on 31 Oct 2026, from the repository record and the adjudication log. The owner made every label and every ruling it describes. Set 1: the rubrics merged in PR #11 (37b6e7f) before the labels merged in PR #12 (0055d07). Each verdict carries its rubric's hash, and every hash matches the one recorded in labels/set1-meta.json, so no rubric changed after labelling or during adjudication. Decision 6: each rubric's boundary example shares an underlying bet with labelled rows (needs_human_correctness: v1 A12; tool_call_accuracy: v1 C08; rule_adherence: v1 C09 and X01), so those rows are in sample for that rubric. Adjudication: the owner ruled on all 40 first-pass disagreements one at a time, each shown with the ticket, the tool calls, the final answer, the run status and the judge's verdict and reason. 17 labels changed, each with the owner's reason recorded in labels/set1-final.jsonl, and every disagreement that remains has a reading in labels/set1-readings.json. The PM seat wrote the readings from the owner's rulings; the note that the judge gave a stock PASS sentence on the seven tool_call rows that changed to PASS is the PM seat's observation, not the owner's. 16 of the 17 changes moved the label to the judge's verdict. The one that did not, needs_human_correctness v1 B01 (PASS to FAIL), created a new disagreement in which the judge passes a row the owner fails. Because the owner saw the judge's verdicts before ruling, the final labels are not blind to the judge and the final agreement figures are optimistic; the first-pass figures are the blind ones, and set 2 is the independent test. The report covers all 40 rows of each rubric; it does not compute the 39/39/38-row held-out figures. Per rubric, every result in this report is in sample, not held out. needs_human_correctness: in sample, because v1 A12 shares its bet with the boundary example and the final labels were adjudicated after the verdicts were seen. tool_call_accuracy: in sample, for the same two reasons, through v1 C08. rule_adherence: in sample, for the same two reasons, through v1 C09 and X01. For each rubric the figures show how closely llama3.1:8b reproduces the owner's labels on these 40 rows; they do not show how it would agree on rows the rubric's examples and the adjudication never touched, and the first-pass figures are the nearest this set comes to that.
